A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SADis and the same Disentangled Stylized Image Generation work. Their main text, equations, references, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original stylization experiments, quantitative baseline comparisons, component and sensitivity ablations, and a 24-participant user study.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds complex-prompt evaluations, alternative-model examples, repeated-generation results and further ablations.

M1.justification: V3 Section 4.3 adds model variants using SD3.5 and FLUX.1-dev with SigLIP and corresponding pretrained adapters. This is a limited architectural extension retaining the CTE/SVD/RegWCT workflow. The more explicit SVD tensor handling does not establish that the original implementation changed.

E1.justification: V3 adds evaluation with complex prompts sampled from DREAMBENCH++ (Appendix E, Table 3), extending the prompt requirements beyond the retained StyleDrop prompts. WikiArt/StyleDrop reference images remain central; same-image references, material transfer, real-image stylization and color-variation scenarios already appeared in v1.

E2.justification: The main image-quality comparison retains the same eight baselines. However, DreamStyler is added to the reported user-study comparison in v3 Table 1; v1 Figure 10 includes only the other seven baselines. The new quantitative benchmark tables reuse the existing image-quality comparator set.

E3.justification: V3 adds a protocol combining 10 complex prompts, 10 color references and 10 texture references for 1,000 images, quantitative same-reference benchmarking, and SD3.5/FLUX.1-dev configurations. It introduces runtime evaluation under reported 50-step DDIM conditions and removes KID from the retained RegWCT-scale and gamma sensitivity evaluations. The original 4,000-image SDXL benchmark remains unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 substantially expands analysis with beta sensitivity (Table 8), alternative attention-layer injection configurations (Appendix H, Table 9), sampling stability (Table 5), and an additional PCA illustration of image-prompt additivity (Figure 4a). Existing component, noise, timestep, gamma and color-variation analyses are largely retained, although two sensitivity studies lose KID reporting.

E5.justification: Unlike v1, v3 Appendix E explicitly reports five sampling rounds of 1,000 images each and provides per-round metrics in Table 5. This adds limited repeatability reporting; seeds, confidence intervals and significance tests remain unspecified. It does not establish an increase in runs for the original benchmark.

E6.justification: V3 adds results for complex prompts, same-image references, sampling rounds, beta and attention-layer ablations, runtime, and MMDiT examples. Original Table 1 image-quality scores remain unchanged, but Table 2 changes SADis MS-SWD from 5.57 to 7.27 without explanation, conflicting with Table 1. Two sensitivity tables lose KID rows. User-study shares also change, such as combined preference from 40% to 37.84%, alongside adding DreamStyler; this is not a comparable-setting performance decline.

T1.justification: The underlying extraction equations, SVD reweighting rule, assumptions about dominant singular values, and appendix WCT formulas are retained. V3 adds tensor-shape explanations and an empirical PCA discussion, but no new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: introducing DisIG, identifying image-prompt additivity, providing training-free color-texture disentanglement through SADis, and outperforming existing stylization methods. Their scientific meaning is substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 explicitly interprets its MMDiT/SigLIP examples as evidence that SADis is not restricted to U-Net or particular CLIP encoders. It also discusses beta's color-texture trade-off and sampling stability. Existing limitations concerning content/identity consistency and object-specific color control remain.

D1.justification: V3 specifies tensor dimensions, token-wise concatenation and selection of the original texture tokens after SVD reconstruction. It adds L40s hardware disclosure, timing conditions, and model/adapter access information for the MMDiT variants. A project URL is added, while Appendix A still describes code release as future work; the PDFs do not establish actual availability.

R1.justification: V3 adds references for rectified-flow transformers, SigLIP, DREAMBENCH++, Li et al.'s StyleDiffusion and Dynamic Prompt Learning, while removing Attend-and-Excite, Divide & Bind and One-Prompt-One-Story. It also drops v1's specific claim of being first to apply WCT directly in T2I diffusion latents. The broader positioning against entangled stylization remains.

P1.justification: Most prose and the overall narrative remain recognizable. V3 separates and expands the DisIG problem setup, rewrites the additivity explanation, makes localized language edits, updates author/affiliation information, and appends a NeurIPS checklist. These are limited structural and explanatory revisions rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a single-column NeurIPS layout and substantially reorganizes the displays. It redraws the method diagram, reworks the teaser, merges several existing figures, relocates examples into the appendix, adds PCA and MMDiT displays and new tables, and replaces the user-study pie charts with columns in Table 1.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens the empirical support through complex-prompt and alternative-model evaluations, sampling-stability checks, and direct parameter/layer ablations, while improving implementation and runtime documentation. The net gain is limited by the unexplained Table 2 MS-SWD change from 5.57 to 7.27, which conflicts with Table 1 and weakens the SVD-ablation interpretation, and by removing KID from two sensitivity studies.
